review_scope: Independent visual review of host-captured firstplay manifests and representative frames. No browser or game-source changes were made for this review.
method_limitations: These are short generic automation runs using guessed taps and drags, not observations of children.
The manifests label all post-start frames play even when a tutorial is still open; visual frames, not that label, determine the actual visible phase.
comprehensible records the reviewer's assessment of the visible instructions and controls. It does not certify that a learner understood them.

None of these three firstplay runs records a successful first mathematical action. Separate deliberate real-input playthroughs provide functionality evidence, not independent first-use comprehension evidence.

games.observed: The start CTA is prominent. Tutorial1 explains selecting a numbered fort; tutorial3 explains partitioning 72 into60 and12, overshoot cost, successful-shot undo and rebuild cost. The final frame shows the live cartridge and group controls with a contextual 24×3 =20×3 +4×3 hint; no ammunition was selected and score remains0.
games.first_action_understood_by_reviewer: Choose one cartridge value and one group count, then fire at the selected fort without exceeding its remaining blocks.

confusion_points.point: The three remaining-shot dots are labeled, but the limited-shot planning rule is less prominent in the tutorial than the exact-block rule.
confusion_points.impact: A child could choose several small valid volleys before realizing that the number of shots also matters. Undo and rebuild provide recovery.

confusion_points.point: Large scenery occupies much of the frame while actual loading controls are lower down.
confusion_points.impact: The generic harness tapped the scene repeatedly instead of the cartridge controls. Numbered labels1 and2 identify the actual controls, so this alone does not establish human confusion.

games.observed: The title has a single train-start action. Tutorial1 defines the common whole from0 to1; tutorial3 explains matching destination length and sending the train. The gameplay frame shows goal3/4, an initial1/4 rail, add1/4/add2/4/add3/4 pieces and the train-send button. The last frame is the title again.
games.first_action_understood_by_reviewer: Add fraction rail pieces to the existing track until it matches the destination, then send the train.

confusion_points.point: Each inventory piece has a small ×2 label in addition to its large fraction.
confusion_points.impact: At first glance a learner could read it as multiplying the fraction rather than two available pieces; the neighboring inventory caption says each piece can be used twice.

confusion_points.point: The generic run returned to the title after tapping DOM elements.
confusion_points.impact: The Home control directly returns to title while saving the journey. This is consistent with the harness choosing navigation, not evidence of a broken puzzle or a child abandoning it.

games.confidence: moderate for tutorial text; live first action not observed
games.observed: The start action opens tutorial1 with the worked example1.2 +0.3 +0.4 =1.9 L. Tutorial2 explains matching the bridge target and1.9 =1.90. The final frame remains on tutorial2 with a visible Next button. The manifest shows subsequent scene taps/drags rather than another overlay-dismiss action.
games.first_action_understood_by_reviewer: Continue the explicit tutorial, select one operation from each route row so arrival fuel matches the target, then start driving.

confusion_points.point: During tutorial1, the spotlighted route panel looks interactive while the tutorial is still open.
confusion_points.impact: A learner might tap a route before Next; current planning guards ignore route changes during dialog. The explicit Next button supplies a clear way forward.

confusion_points.point: The generic capture never leaves tutorial2.
confusion_points.impact: Its later taps mostly target the canvas. Because the visible Next action was not activated, this is insufficient evidence for a comprehension failure or a frozen UI.

summary.note: Keep the successful scripted-play evidence and these limited naive-input observations separate in release claims.
